method.residueTest: The state's legal-design memo, its track-registry projection and the national legal decision overlay for the jurisdiction are flattened into one string corpus. Every fragment of 30 normalised characters or more that the corpus already holds is deleted from the normalised text of the family's canonical PDF and participant-instructions.md. What survives in runs of 60 characters or more is what the packet adds to the design.
method.trapOne: Components a production field map declares -- in componentSet, in componentRoutes, and in the role list of each routeSelectionsMade instrument string -- that reports/rendered-artifacts.json does not carry. A declared but unrendered mandatory official form is an official-form-strategy change.
method.trapTwo: Each route's design destination kind against what the rendered packet is captioned to and who it addresses. A clerk destination is treated as a court destination, because the clerk is the court's filing office.
method.assertionTest: Every statutory citation, currency amount and duration on a platform-authored surface is checked for a source in the design corpus. On an official_pdf_fill family the PDF is the state's own form, so only participant-instructions.md is read as a platform assertion.
method.whatIsMeasuredAndWhatIsRead: Every figure in measurements is computed per family by this script. Bucket C and D determinations additionally rest on readings of the design records, carried in the generator's ADJUDICATIONS table with the exact quotation each rests on, because whether an assertion is substantive is a reading and not a computation.
method.fromTheOwnersRule: Fee, waiver, service and self-help text verbatim from the design record surfaces the approved design rather than adding to it. The same text with no source in the design is substantive. Where a family is genuinely ambiguous it is classified C, because wrongly claiming coverage attaches an approval to something nobody approved while wrongly withholding it costs only a review.

counts.consolidation: 3 bucket C families reduce to 2 distinct substantive questions; 0 bucket D families reduce to 0 distinct product-treatment questions.

Whether any clerk assesses a fee for a chapter 310-A motion in practice. Whether a chapter 310-A sealing order removes the case from Maine's public court record search. 15 M.R.S. § 2265 makes the conviction confidential criminal history record information and restricts dissemination by a criminal justice agency, and § 2264(6) makes the State Bureau of Identification amend its records. designReleaseBlockers.question: Whether the Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72 fee reaches a given petition. The section reads: 'A filing fee of One Hundred Fifty Dollars ($150.00) is hereby levied on each petition to expunge an offense under Section 99-19-71 to be collected by the circuit clerk', distributed $100 to the Judicial System Operation Fund, $40 to the District Attorneys Operation Fund and $10 retained by the circuit clerk. Last amended by Laws, 1st Ex. Sess. 2017, ch. 7, § 12; no enacted amendment through 2026. Two things remain unresolved on its face and are NOT resolved by construction here. First, the trigger is 'each petition to expunge AN OFFENSE under Section 99-19-71': a § 99-19-71(4) non-conviction petition is a petition under § 99-19-71 but is not a petition to expunge an offence, because there is no conviction, and the statute does not settle it either way. Second, the collection mechanism names the CIRCUIT CLERK, which does not map onto § 99-19-71(1) or (4) petitions filed in justice or municipal court. Sections 9-11-15(3), 21-23-7(6), 99-15-26, 63-11-30, 41-29-150 and 67-3-70 sit outside § 99-19-71 and the fee does not reach them by its terms; none of those sections specifies a fee of its own. The packet therefore publishes NO fee amount on any track and instructs the participant to confirm the filing fee, and any pauper's-affidavit route, with the clerk of the court before filing.

Local practice in the twenty-one circuit court districts other than the Fourth, and in every municipal and justice court, was not surveyed. Both the review and the Fourth District materials establish that districts maintain their own petition and order preferences and that some expect the district attorney to sign the order as approved as to form before the judge will sign. This is a scaling constraint rather than a legal one: the statutory mechanism is the same statewide, but the accepted document and the practical gate vary. Every Mississippi track therefore carries localFormOverride and a mandatory clerk-contact instruction.

Trafficking-survivor relief under Miss. Code Ann. § 97-3-54.6, as amended by 2026 HB 1546 effective 1 July 2026, is recorded here as a separately-listed matter and NOT as a tenth normalized source node, because neither the adopted Batch 2 memorandum nor the authoritative source crosswalk lists it among Mississippi's nine core adult slots. The enrolled text was read: new § 97-3-54.6(6) lets the sentencing court, at any time after a conviction or adjudication of delinquency of a misdemeanour or a felony not classified as a crime of violence under § 97-3-2, expunge on appropriate motion where it finds by a preponderance that participation in the offence occurred during the period the person was being trafficked and was the direct result of that trafficking; official documentation from a federal, state or local government agency creates a presumption but is not required; and new § 97-3-54.6(7)(b) provides that neither failing to raise the trafficking affirmative defence nor the court's finding on it affects the ability to file under subsection (6). This relief is broader and faster than ordinary § 99-19-71 conviction expungement, so screening for it belongs on every intake. Whether it becomes a normalized node requires an express crosswalk or memorandum instruction.

Whether a Mississippi court will apply the three-year period in 2026 HB 1546 to a petition filed on or after 1 July 2026 that concerns a conviction completed before that date. The enrolled act carries NO applicability clause: SECTION 4 provides only that the act takes effect from and after 1 July 2026, and nothing limits it to convictions entered or sentences completed after that date. The ordinary reading is that the amended waiting period governs any petition filed on or after the effective date, which is how the product applies it, but no Mississippi appellate authority construing the amendment exists yet.

Whether an expungement obtained on the non-conviction track or the first-offender misdemeanour track counts against the one-felony-expunction allowance in § 99-19-71(2)(a). The enrolled text limits the allowance to 'one (1) felony expunction under this paragraph (a)', which on its face reaches only paragraph (a) felony expunctions, and the review reaches the same conclusion. The packet encodes that reading and tells participants their non-conviction expungement does not spend the felony allowance.

Whether any circuit district requires the district attorney's 'approved as to form' signature as a practical precondition to the judge signing the order. Both archived Fourth District orders carry that block. It may be dispositive of whether the product can serve a district at all, and it is a negotiation LegalEase does not conduct.
